artificial

/ar-tih-FISH-uhl/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Artificial means made by human skill or effort rather than occurring naturally; not genuine or spontaneous.

The hospital lobby's cheerful plants turned out to be entirely artificial, requiring no water or sunlight at all.

Example

When the town's only lake dried up during the drought, city officials trucked in thousands of gallons of water to fill a newly built artificial pond nearby, hoping to keep the local wildlife from leaving the area entirely.

The pond didn't form naturally through rainfall or a spring — humans built and filled it deliberately, which is exactly the distinction "artificial" makes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fabricated: Fabricated means built or assembled by people, and it often carries a hint of dishonesty — a fabricated alibi is an invented one. Artificial is more neutral: it marks something as human-made rather than natural without accusing anyone of deception.

simulated: Simulated means made to reproduce the look or experience of the real thing — simulated leather, a simulated flight. Artificial only says humans made it; simulated adds that it is actively mimicking something. An artificial pond is real water; simulated rain is not rain at all.

unnatural: Unnatural condemns: it says something departs from nature in a way that feels wrong or disturbing. Artificial stays descriptive and neutral — an artificial sweetener is simply human-made, while calling a flavor unnatural passes judgment on it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

natural: occurring in nature, without human creation

genuine: real and authentic, not manufactured or faked

Where it sits · how far from nature the origin is — man-made → artificial → synthetic

man-made vs. artificial: Man-made is milder than artificial: a man-made chair or dam is simply built by people, while calling something artificial goes further, hinting it is not genuine or natural.

synthetic vs. artificial: Synthetic sits at the far end from nature: a synthetic material is chemically manufactured, often to imitate a natural substance — a more specific, technical claim than artificial's general human-made.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — arti-

Root — arti-: skill, craft (Latin ars, artis; the linking i joins it to the next piece)

Root — fic-

Root — fic-: to make (Latin facere)

Suffix — -ial

Suffix — -ial: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: "artificial" literally means "relating to something made by skill" -- built from arti- ("skill, craft," from Latin ars, artis, with a linking i) + fic- ("to make," from Latin facere) + -ial ("relating to"), it describes anything produced through human craft rather than occurring on its own.

Word Choice

neutral

Artificial is a neutral, descriptive word — it simply distinguishes human-made from naturally occurring, without necessarily implying anything is fake or deceptive (compare 'imitation,' which more strongly suggests deception).
